# 63. AGMINER search strategy

Do not use a giant Cartesian grid.

Preferred broad sampler:

```text
scipy.stats.qmc.Sobol
```

or Latin hypercube.

Suggested initial search allocation:

```text
~60% global exploration
~30% local exploitation
~10% novelty/boundary exploration
```

Use continuation/warm starts for nearby nonlinear BVPs.

Do not let the search collapse into one local basin.

---

# 64. AGMINER persistent failure memory

This is mandatory.

Every candidate receives a deterministic fingerprint based on:

```text
family ID
family version
physics/action version
energy-ledger version
payload-benchmark version
canonical parameter vector
```

Before solving:

```text
LOOK UP CANDIDATE
```

If already in a terminal state:

```text
SKIP
```

The exact candidate must not be repeatedly recomputed.

Above-10-GJ points are permanent objective failures for that exact theory/version.

---

# 65. Exact rejection versus region rejection

One failed point does not prove nearby points fail.

Distinguish:

```text
EXACT_REJECTION
```

from:

```text
PROVEN_REGION_REJECTION
```

A region may only be excluded when supported by something such as:

```text
analytic lower bound
monotonic theorem
ghost domain
invalid coupling domain
range theorem
no-go relation
```

A mere 12-GJ sample does not prove a nearby point cannot reach 9 GJ.

Use local failures to change sampling priority, not invent no-go theorems.

---

# 66. Numerical unresolved is not physics rejection

If a BVP fails:

1. try the normal seed;
2. make one cheap alternate/continuation attempt;
3. if both fail, classify:

```text
NUMERICALLY_UNRESOLVED
```

Do not call it physically impossible.

Do not retry it endlessly within the same campaign.

By contrast, an explicitly computed:

```text
E > 10 GJ
```

is a real objective rejection.

---

Use compact machine-readable failure codes rather than giant repeated logs.

Examples:

Do not store large repeated text error messages for every candidate.

```text
< 100 MB per major campaign

< 10 MB
```

# 74. Multiprocessing design

Workers should **not** independently write SQLite.

Architecture:

```text
MAIN PROCESS
    scheduler
    database writer
    result aggregator
    progress
    stop control

WORKER PROCESSES
    evaluate candidates
    return compact dictionaries
```

Only the main process writes persistent database state.

This avoids lock contention and mixed/corrupted logs.

Default workers:

```text
max(1, CPU_COUNT - 1)
```

with configuration override.

Leave a core available for the OS, editor, and database writer.

---

# 75. Memory policy

After every ordinary candidate:

```text
extract compact observables
save only if finalist
delete large arrays
release solution
```

Warm-start caches must be bounded.

Suggested:

```text
MAX_WARM_STARTS_PER_WORKER = 8
```

Do not allow a long-running campaign to accumulate every solved profile in RAM.

# 76. Candidate time limits

AGMINER is intended to test many candidates cheaply.

Initial conceptual targets:

```text
Tier 0:
milliseconds

Tier 1 target:
a few seconds

Tier 1 timeout:
~15 s

Tier 1C cheap stability:
~30 s

Tier 2:
separate slower queue
```

Timeout:

```text
NUMERICALLY_UNRESOLVED
```

not physics failure.

Thresholds may be adjusted after real timing measurements.

# 77. Energy short-circuiting

Where mathematically valid, stop evaluation early if a monotonic positive partial energy already exceeds 10 GJ.

Example:

```text
PARTIAL UNAVOIDABLE POSITIVE ENERGY
> 10 GJ
```

then:

```text
FULL CONSERVATIVE ENERGY
> 10 GJ
```

and the candidate can be terminated immediately.

Only use this if the remaining ledger contributions cannot lower the conservative complete inventory.

Do not misuse it when cancellations or alternate ledgers matter.

---

# 78. 10-GJ boundary tests

Mandatory regression tests:

```text
9.999999999 GJ
→ PASS ENERGY GATE

10.000000000 GJ
→ PASS ENERGY GATE

10.000000001 GJ
→ REJECT
```

Do not create a "physical tolerance" that silently permits values over 10 GJ.

Numerical uncertainty is a separate issue.

---

# 79. Borderline coarse energy handling

For coarse estimates, store:

```text
E_ESTIMATE
E_LOWER
E_UPPER
```

Suggested logic:

```text
if E_LOWER > 10 GJ:
    reject immediately

if reliable E_ESTIMATE > 10 GJ:
    reject exact coarse model

if E_ESTIMATE <= 10 GJ
and E_UPPER > 10 GJ:
    mark borderline
    refine before shortlist
```

A certification-ready model must ultimately have:

```text
REFINED CONSERVATIVE COMPLETE ENERGY <= 10 GJ
```

with adequate numerical convergence.

---

# 80. Model robustness categories

Sub-10-GJ models should be prioritized approximately by energy class:

```text
<5 GJ
excellent energy class

5–8 GJ
strong

8–9.5 GJ
marginal but interesting

9.5–10 GJ
borderline
```

All may survive.

Lower-energy models receive search/certification priority.

# 82. Safe manual stop requirement

The user explicitly added a required build-plan stub:

> AGMINER must be stoppable whenever desired, without losing completed results.

Manual interruption is a normal operating condition.

Required sequence:

```text
STOP REQUEST
    ↓
STOP DISPATCHING NEW CANDIDATES
    ↓
FINISH OR SAFELY CANCEL CURRENT SHORT TASKS
    ↓
FLUSH PENDING RESULTS TO SQLITE
    ↓
CHECKPOINT SAMPLER POSITION
    ↓
REBUILD PARETO / TOP SUMMARIES
    ↓
CHECKPOINT/TRUNCATE WAL AS APPROPRIATE
    ↓
EXIT CLEANLY
```

```text
explicit AGMINER stop command
```


While inspecting results, the user should be able to pin a candidate:


# 88. Crash recovery

On startup:

```text
read database

identify candidates left RUNNING
```

# 11. THE NEW EXACT AGMINER FACTORIZATION

The V6 redesign generalized Introspective into the miner.

For a candidate with useful source density/current `J` and finite-payload kernel `K`, define:

```math
A_{\rm net}
=
\left|\int J K\,dV\right|,
```

```math
A_{\rm gross}
=
\int |J K|\,dV,
```

```math
C_{\rm cancel}
=
\frac{A_{\rm gross}}{A_{\rm net}},
```

```math
Q_{\rm abs}
=
\int |J|\,dV,
```

```math
q_{\rm prod}
=
\frac{Q_{\rm abs}}{E_{\rm prod}},
```

```math
K_{\rm eff}
=
\frac{A_{\rm gross}}{Q_{\rm abs}},
```

and:

```math
f_{\rm prod}
=
\frac{E_{\rm prod}}{E_{\rm complete}}.
```

Then:

```math
\boxed{
\frac{A_{\rm net}}{E_{\rm complete}}
=
q_{\rm prod}
K_{\rm eff}
\frac{f_{\rm prod}}{C_{\rm cancel}}
}
```

This factorization is now a central AGMINER design principle.

It means we should not demand that one coupling produce every order of magnitude.

Useful improvements can come independently from:

```text
intrinsic charge / productive joule
productive participation
payload-kernel leverage
cancellation reduction
scaffold amortization
```

But they must be measured inside the **same physical candidate**.

Historical gains must never simply be multiplied together.

# 14. Current literature knowledge added this session

## Brax & Valageas — Goldstone / kinetic-conformal models

Important lessons:

* matter may couple universally through a kinetic-conformal Jordan metric;
* canonical scalar self-energy can remain positive;
* derivative conformal response is a real field-theory class;
* attractive or repulsive fifth-force behavior can occur depending on the coupling function;
* their published minimal `A=1+chi` has the wrong static spacelike sign for our localized branch.

Use this paper for **universal metric action provenance**, not as proof of our exact outward sign.

## Zumalacárregui & García-Bellido

Important for derivative-conformal transformations and invertibility.

For:

```math
\tilde g=C(X)g,
```

invertibility requires nonzero `C` and nonzero kinetic Jacobian eigenvalue such as:

```math
\lambda_K=C-C_XX.
```

Published derivative-conformal examples tested in V13 had the wrong outward static sign but demonstrated the transformation class.

## Ikeda, Iyonaga & Kobayashi

Shift-symmetric scalar-tensor stars can use a scalar with linear time dependence while maintaining static geometry.

This confirms that:

```text
TIME_DEPENDENT_SHIFT_BACKGROUND
```

is a genuine theorem evasion rather than an invented loophole.

It remains secondary to the static zero-net derivative-source route.

## Jiang et al. 2024

Important results carried forward:

* dimension-8 shift-symmetric scalar/matter operator basis;
* scalar `j=0` and traceless `j=2` sectors;
* leading forward positivity constrains selected `j=2` coefficients;
* scalar `O1/O3` are not killed by that leading `s²` constraint;
* `O1` does not generate `O3` in the quoted one-loop QED running;
* positive-C1 UV sign example exists.

However their explicit positive-C1 UV example also produces:


and therefore cannot simply be adopted.

Do not reopen the already closed massive-spin-2 realization just because this sign example exists.

## Brax et al. derivative-conformal collider work

A derivative-conformal model has collider-context limits around ~200 GeV in a particular contact-EFT treatment.

Do **not** directly apply that number to the present ~24-keV metric-scale candidate.

Our EFT ceases to be valid far below collider hard energies, so applying a contact bound above its cutoff is not self-consistent.

This makes a low-scale UV completion mandatory rather than proving safety.

## Axial-background / axion wavefunction literature

Carry forward that fermion derivative/axial couplings generate scalar/axion wavefunction renormalization and nontrivial one-loop vacuum effective actions.

The renormalized Dirac sea must eventually be calculated.

# 77. CURRENT BEST-CASE RESEARCH NARRATIVE

The strongest scientifically defensible narrative entering the next session is:

> General relativity itself permits true local gravitational repulsion from positive-energy stress, but its absolute 1/G energy scaling is impractical. Introspective analysis showed that dramatic source-efficiency gains require high productive participation, strong finite-payload kernel leverage, and low cancellation, but those gains alone do not remove the GR energy burden. The 031 scalar-metric program demonstrated that new metric interactions can reduce the required energy enormously, but its tested ultralight scalar lacked quantum protection. AGMINER then found a hidden-axial kinetic-conformal architecture whose finite-payload partial energy reached ~59.42 kJ and whose support-friendly realization reached ~3.68 MJ. That implementation was ultimately ruled out by a low-energy off-state quantum material force and an exact empirical/energy non-overlap. Subsequent time-gradient disformal variants showed that outward sign and low local field energy can persist in structurally different operators, but the simplest stationary and unprotected localized realizations were killed by cosmology/invertibility or naturalness/energy. Ordinary-stress derivative hypermomentum was then ruled out by a fixed dipole-moment theorem, finite-payload response, and inverse-square-law constraints. The current frontier is therefore much sharper: seek a genuinely independent microscopic intrinsic hypermomentum charge, determine whether it excites a healthy propagating nonmetricity mode, and require that this mode act universally on neutral matter through a physical metric before any expensive scan.
